title: Ecosystem Surge Detector & Prospector Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, reproducible playbook and automation layer that detects sudden ecosystem 'surges' (new model releases, rapid adoption, pricing shocks, or feature breakthroughs) and surfaces prioritized recommendations for procurement, engineering validation, and go-to-market experiments. This ticket captures the PM workstream: definition of surge signals, scoring heuristics, operational thresholds, alert surface, owner flows, and minimum viable integrations with Console and Linear.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Automated pipeline detects and scores new model release events within 24 hours for 90% of tracked sources. 2) Weekly prioritized watchlist delivered to PM/AE/Research with top 10 emergent items and succinct rationale. 3) False-positive rate for high-confidence alerts (score >= 85) <= 20% after first 6 weeks. 4) Auto-created Linear ticket template for top-priority surges populates required metadata and links to evidence. 5) Dashboard with trend sparklines and evolution of top 50 candidates is viewable in Console-restricted to internal users.
deliverables: Spec doc: surge signal taxonomy and scoring rubric
Scheduled crawlers and ingestion jobs for 12 sources
Batch scoring engine (novelty + adoption + enterprise-fit heuristics)
Slack alert kitchen sink + per-team channels
Runbook for manual triage and ownership rotation
signal_sources: Primary signal sources to instrument: Hugging Face model/hub release feeds, PapersWithCode new entries, arXiv new model papers/titles, GitHub repo creation/releases and stars velocity, Docker Hub image pulls (if available), cloud marketplace new model offerings, vendor blog release posts, pricing change announcements, community channels (HF Discord, X/Twitter), reddit r/MachineLearning peaks, and selective client-reported model onboarding requests. Secondary signals: benchmark appearance (evals), quantization/compile toolchain artifacts, and early enterprise trial mentions.
scoring_rubric_summary: Composite score = weighted sum: Novelty(25) + Adoption Velocity(30) + Integration Friction (negative weight, -15) + Enterprise Fit (20) + Economic Delta (10). Each component normalized 0-100. Novelty favors architectures or features not in our catalog. Adoption Velocity uses 7-day growth of stars/downloads/mentions. Integration Friction estimates quantization and kernel compatibility from metadata heuristics. Enterprise Fit proxies include licensing, regional availability, and documented SLAs.
operational_flow: 1) Ingestor jobs run hourly; 2) Batch scoring runs every 6 hours with top-N deduplication; 3) High-confidence items (score >=85) produce: a Slack ping to #pm-intel and an auto-created Linear ticket in a PM queue; 4) Medium items appear only in Console watchlist and weekly digest; 5) Triage rotation: PM on-call evaluates high items within 48 hours and assigns follow-ups (research spike, bench, procurement inquiry).
initial_prioritization_rules: - Score >= 85: High — immediate ticket + Slack alert. - 70-84: Medium — add to weekly digest and watchlist. - 50-69: Low — monitor automatically, surface if growth accelerates. - <50: Noise, store history for trend analysis.
metrics_to_track: Time-to-detect (hours), Precision@k for high-confidence alerts, Recall vs. curated release list, Weekly workload generated (auto tickets), Time from alert to validated bench, False positive rate, Mean score per source, Cost to run crawlers per day.
privacy_and_risk_notes: Ingest only public signals and vendor-published announcements. For any customer-supplied intelligence, ensure we have permission to process and store; route PMs to Solutions Eng for handling PII. No internal telemetry (customer data) will be included without explicit legal/SEC signoff.
runbook_notes: Triage checklist: 1) Confirm source evidence links. 2) Quick compatibility probe: check quantized model availability, max-seq, common tokenizer. 3) Estimate bench cost (GPU hours) and assign bench owner. 4) If enterprise-fit score high, prepare quick procurement conversation template. 5) Close ticket if noise or escalate SaaS offering/DM to Partnerships.
milestones_and_timeline: Week 0-2: finalize spec and source integrations (HF, arXiv, GH); Week 3-4: implement ingestors + scoring MVP and Console stub; Week 5: connect Linear auto-ticketing and Slack; Week 6-8: iterate scoring weights, run manual triage and measure precision, expand sources; Week 9-12: harden dashboard, RBAC, alert throttling and SLA for detection. Goal: soft launch to internal PM/Research by 2026-04-15.
notes_on_acceptance_testing: Create a golden dataset of 40 historical model release events across different channels (big vendor announcements, small repo surges, quantization-focused releases). Run the pipeline and compute detection latency and scoring rank. Host two blinded triage sessions with PM/Research to validate signal usefulness.
